transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Well, I suppose occupational health sent me. I've gotten into this pattern lately where I just push breakfast and lunch aside. I'm a biological scientist, so during long lab runs or when I'm doing exhibition work, it's easy to just keep going. And then, by the time I actually sit down to eat, I keep it to something very small and controlled. They seemed concerned about it.
When you limit how much you eat, is it because you fear gaining weight or feel concerned about your body shape?

Yes, I suppose it is. I... well, I do weigh myself regularly. And honestly, if the scale goes up even a fraction, I feel this sharp panic. It just feels like I’m losing the discipline I’ve worked so hard to maintain. So keeping my food intake small and controlled is how I make sure that doesn't happen.
Has a clinician ever told you that your current body weight is significantly low for your age and height?

Well, no clinician has actually said that to me yet. I mean, I know my clothes are definitely looser lately, and the numbers on the scale have just kept drifting down. But honestly, part of me just sees that as a sign that I'm staying focused. It feels like proof that I'm not letting the chaos at work spill over and affect my body. So, I haven't really thought of it as being significantly low, just... controlled.
Has your current weight become significantly low for your height?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. Like I said, no doctor has told me that. I know I've lost weight, but I don't really know what counts as "significantly low" for my height. I haven't really looked into the exact numbers or BMI charts or anything like that. I just know the number on the scale is lower than it used to be.

I... I'd actually prefer not to say the exact number, if that's okay. I know I mentioned that I track it, but... saying the actual figure out loud makes me pretty uncomfortable. I just know it's lower than my usual baseline.
Would you say that your current weight is below the minimum healthy range for your height?

I guess I don't really think of it in terms of a minimum healthy range. Like I mentioned before, I just know my clothes are a lot looser and the scale keeps going down. But to me, that just means I'm staying focused. It's like... it shows I'm keeping control over myself, even when everything at the lab is so chaotic. So I haven't really thought about whether it's below a certain healthy mark, just that it's where I want it to be right now.
Have you had episodes when you ate an unusually large amount of food and felt unable to control your eating?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't really have moments where I eat a large amount of food or feel out of control with my eating. It's actually the opposite for me—I'm very careful and controlled about what I eat.
Has a healthcare professional ever told you that your current weight is medically underweight?

Yes, my primary care doctor did say something like that recently. I know she and a few other people are concerned, but... I honestly think they're overstating it. I mean, I'm still functioning fine. I'm still doing all my experiments at the lab and working my normal hours. So I just don't feel like my weight is medically dangerous, regardless of what the standard charts say.
Have you intentionally made yourself vomit after eating?
No, I haven't done that. I don't make myself throw up. Like I said, I just strictly control what I eat in the first place, so I don't feel the need to do anything like that.
